turns.assessment: The two earliest root-facing alarms are simultaneous AMP_INPUT_LOS at the second amplifiers on S06→S19 and S06→S21. Their upstream boosters retained normal input/output power and all pump-current telemetry remained unchanged, localizing the losses to the fibre immediately after the boosters rather than to an amplifier or ROADM failure. This strongly indicates a common excavation/cable event cutting both outgoing spans, but the evidence does not establish which cut interrupts svc026, and no shared duct element is named for a safe repair commitment.

proposals.rationale: O1 reports complete input loss at amp1 on S06→S19 while the preceding booster retained normal input/output power and amplifier pump currents did not change. That pattern localizes a hard optical break to the intervening fibre span.

O2 reports complete input loss at amp1 on S06→S21 while amp0 retained normal input/output power and pump currents remained stable. The simultaneous event on S06→S19 is consistent with excavation cutting multiple cables in a common duct.
An extreme added span loss could also drive amp1 below its detection threshold, although the abrupt critical LOS on two lines is more characteristic of cable cuts.
S06 is the sole stated common dependency, but a ROADM blockage should reduce power at the outgoing booster; unchanged S06→S21 amp0 input/output power argues strongly against it.

score.why: truth not in the reported set
